Commonwealth and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called for doubling India-UK bilateral
trade by 2030. Mr Goyal said this while addressing the JETCO business plenary, under the 16th
session of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee, JETCO, in New Delhi today.
The minister reaffirmed the country's commitment to deepening India-UK economic cooperation
through sustained engagement, stronger institutional mechanisms, and enhanced collaboration.
He said this will unlock new opportunities for businesses in both the countries.
We can create greater corridors of cooperation in fintech, insurance,
cross-border payments, transition finance, trade finance.
We should really be looking at both these centres becoming one connected pathway
towards greater progress and prosperity.
And finally, healthcare and consumer sectors,
whether it is generic pharma on the Indian side or branded pharmaceutical innovative products
on the UK side, our diagnostics, food processing and consumer goods. India's affordability
and Britain's discovery together can become a force multiplier."
Commerce and Industry Minister also addressed the Delhi Dialogue to 2026 in New Delhi today.

Centre has urged all states and union territories to ensure the prominent display of rates
charged for services and facilities offered by clinical establishments.
The move aims to empower patients to make informed health care decisions,
provisions, prevent billing-related disputes, and strengthen trust in health care services.
Union Health Secretary Punea Saleela Shavasthav has written a letter to the chief secretaries
of all states and UTs in this regard. More from our correspondent.
In the letter, the Union Health Secretary has called for a review of compliance with
applicable regulatory provisions and appropriate measures to ensure that information on
health care service charges is clearly visible and easily accessible to patients
and their attendants.
The states have also been urged to facilitate transparent display of package rates for international
patients visiting India on medical and IU's visas.
This would enable international patients to make informed choices, help minimize pricing
and billing-related grievances and further strengthen India's possession as a trusted
destination for medical and IU's care.
The initiative also reinforces the central government's commitment to making healthcare
here, delivery more transparent, accountable and responsive to patients' needs. With the
and Maharashtra in New Delhi today. The meeting held a discussion on various issues concerning
sugarcane farmers, including ground-level challenges, discrepancies in recovery figures reported by
sugar mills, weighing procedures, wastage, laboratory testing, and crop insurance.
With the aim of providing immediate relief to farmers, Union Ministers Shivraj Singh Chauhan
and Pralaj Joshi made a major announcement regarding the formation of a special high-level
Joint Committee within a week. This committee will comprise representatives from the Central
Government, State Governments of Karnataka and Maharashtra, Farmers Organisations and
sugar mills as well as subject matter expert scientists. The committee will meticulously
examine every technical aspect related to the timing of sugarcane harvesting, scientific
recovery parameters, modern laboratory testing systems and the accuracy of weighing.
It will submit its recommendations to the government within a stipulated time frame.
This is Aakash Varni giving you the news.

Responding to IndiaBlock's demand for a meeting, Justice Surikant said he had received a letter
yesterday requesting an appointment and had replied last night, explaining why he

The doors of the Supreme Court are open to everyone. Any person, whether an ordinary

the law and the legal framework. I received the letter yesterday and replied to it last
night, and I have cited the reasons for expressing my inability to meet. I have
maintain the confidentiality of the letters. The BJP has accused the Congress of attacking
constitutional institutions over the years, alleging that the party blames these institutions
for its electoral defeats, addressing a press conference at party headquarters in New Delhi
today. Union Minister and senior BJP leader Shivraj Singh Johan alleged that the Congress
is attempting to return to power by discrediting institutions rather than winning the support
of the people.
Delhi Police has designated three new venues for protests and demonstrations – Ramleela
Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi. In an order, Delhi Police Commissioner
Anurag Kumar announced that Janthar Manthar has been denotified as a designated protest
site. The Union Home Ministry had constituted a committee to identify suitable alternative
venues to ensure citizens' right to organise protests and demonstrations.
This is Aakash Varni here, listening to News at 9.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Siddhe Siva and a relentless commitment that continues, guided
by this vision for Seva and Sushasin, the government has been ceaselessly working towards
achieving the goal of a vikasit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment,
this dedication is transforming lives. Today in our special series, we bring you an instance of
how this vision has been translated into action through the FTI policy.
India's foreign direct investment policy has undergone major reforms over the past decade
with the government liberalizing sectoral rules to attract greater foreign investment into the
country. The government has progressively liberalized FDI norms in key sectors. Foreign
investment up to 74% is permitted in defense and 100% in telecom, insurance, and a space sector.
The country has received a record over $748 billion in FDI between 2014 and 2025.
The number of source countries investing in India also rose from 89 to 112.
Addressing the Rojganmela in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted that today more than 100 countries are investing in India through FDI.
Today India is becoming a big manufacturing power.
Electronics, medicines, vaccines, defence, auto.
In many such sectors, India's production and export.
Both of them are becoming more advanced.
Chief Economic Advisor of Government of India V. Anant Nagaswaran said that India has
opened up several sectors including space, drones, defence and insurance to foreign investment.
We are now trying to focus on global value change, number one, number two, we have opened
up many sectors for foreign investment, whether it is space, drones, defense, the insurance
sector, for example, and the Prime Minister also has spoken about nuclear energy generation
to be open to the private sector and foreign asset sector.
So we are continuing to make several sectors of the Indian economy open to foreign investment.
And third, we are pursuing deregulation, which is always going to make investment easier,
whether it is domestic or origin."
The FDI policy reforms reflect India's efforts to create a more investor-friendly environment,
simplified investment procedures, and to strengthen its position as a preferred global
investment destination.
With Dipendra, this is Anand Kumar for Akharswani News, Delhi.
Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhar Bhat today inaugurated the Bricks 3 Eater Festival
to 2026 in New Delhi. The festival will be held till Wednesday. Speaking on the occasion,
Mr. Shikharvat said, at a time when the world is witnessing geopolitical tensions,
conflicts and growing uncertainties, culture can play a vital role in fostering dialogue,
building trust and promoting global harmony.
In a world increasingly divided by differences, how do we cultivate the understanding necessary
for a shared and peaceful future. Political dialogue is indispensable. Economic cooperation
is essential. Diplomacy remains the corner state of international relations. But there
is another dimension of engagement that deserves our sustained attention, the dimension of
culture. Culture enables societies to understand one another."
Talking exclusively to Akash Rani, news director of the National School of Drama, Chitranjan
Tripathi said that the three-day festival will feature 10 theater groups presenting
11 plays. Participating countries are India, Thailand, Indonesia, Russia, Vietnam, Iran,
South Africa, Kazakhstan and Ethiopia. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics has been awarded
to American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for developing macroeconomic
models that help policymakers stabilize economies during booms and recessions.
The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said their work has strengthened the theoretical
basis for fiscal and monetary policies and improved government's and central bank's
ability to respond to economic fluctuations.
